comparison_policy.event_order: sequence/port order exact unless event is explicitly abstracted
comparison_policy.cycle: not comparable until a fresh RTL trace records observation edges and end-to-end latency. GEM5 callbacks are now cycle-parameterized; its diagnostic dual-clock profile uses tile=2 ns and system/AXI=4 ns, but re-scaled local-memory delays are not RTL measurements.

dualclock_event_domains.rule: In venus-rtl-16x128-dualclock-rebase, tile-origin events are checked on 2 ns edges and scheduler-owned events on 4 ns edges. This is a GEM5 phase invariant, not an RTL CDC proof.

implemented_artifacts: symbolic fire_plan generated only from the L1 ELF task container and global_para
symbolic return_plan generated only from output_num
rtl_observed_dma retained only as comparison evidence
l1_scheduler_dma_contract.fire_plan_rule: code, optional nonzero data, then task descriptors in descriptor-index order; fid is runtime issue ordinal rather than a descriptor field
l1_scheduler_dma_contract.dynamic_dmt_rule: type-0 source/length and type-4 packed pointer resolve only after producer return DMA completion and DMT commit; they must not be backfilled from an RTL trace into GEM5 behavior
l1_scheduler_dma_contract.return_rule: retid slots are static from output_num, but tile-local source, length and DMT destination are runtime values
l1_scheduler_dma_contract.rtl_dma_dump_timestamp: dma_func_wrapper samples dma_go_i; this is DMA command acceptance, not responder ACK, AXI first beat, or DMA completion
l1_scheduler_dma_contract.current_status: L1 issue-order/routing is checkable; GEM5 still lacks asynchronous DMA completion/DMT-commit lifecycle, so L1 timing and L2 are not passed

first_divergence_order: fire/return count and logical slot/descriptor order
fire routing: source space, destination tile-local address and resolved length
first inbound DMA completion or DMT commit order
first cycle difference after timebase normalization
